He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]]. Williams was drafted 27th overall in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]]. He had a breakout season in [[2021–22 NBA season|2021–22]], which saw him being named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] and reaching the [[NBA Finals]] as the Celtics' starting center. ==High |title=Robert Williams is SEC Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.shreveporttimes.com/story/sports/college/2017/03/07/robert-williams-sec-defensive-player-year/98852388/ |url-status=live |access-date=July 18, 2017 |work=shreveporttimes.com |language=en}} after averaging 11.9 points and a team-high 8.2 rebounds per game as a freshman in 2016–17. On March 21, despite being credited as a potential first-round lottery player, Williams decided to forgo the [[2017 NBA draft]] and stay for another season at Texas A&M.{{Cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2698025-robert-williams-announces-return-to-texas-am-will-forego-2017-nba-draft|title=Robert Williams Announces Return to Texas A&M, Will Forgo 2017 NBA Draft|last=Nathan|first=Alec|work=Bleacher Report|access-date=July 18, 2017|language=en-US|archive-date=July 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723184949/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2698025-robert-williams-announces-return-to-texas-am-will-forego-2017-nba-draft|url-status=live|date=March 21, 2017}} Following Texas A&M's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA men's basketball tournament]], Williams announced his intention to forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he was expected to be a first-round selection.{{Cite news|url=https://www.shreveporttimes.com/story/sports/college/2018/03/23/former-north-caddo-star-robert-williams-turning-pro/454834002/|title=Former North Caddo star Robert Williams turning pro|access-date=March 23, 2018|language=en-US|archive-date=July 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723190423/https://www.shreveporttimes.com/story/sports/college/2018/03/23/former-north-caddo-star-robert-williams-turning-pro/454834002/|url-status=live|work=shreveporttimes.com|last=Ferrell|first=Scott|date=March 23, 2018}} Williams was viewed as a potential lottery pick for the 2017 and 2018 NBA drafts. ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2018–2023)=== Come the 2018 NBA draft, instead of being a lottery pick, Williams fell to the 27th overall pick where he was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] due to concerns about his work ethic. On July 5, 2018, the Boston Celtics signed Williams.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-robert-williams|title=Celtics Sign Robert Williams|date=July 5, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 5, 2018|archive-date=November 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109023716/https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-robert-williams|url-status=live|last=George|first=Kyle}} Williams did not initially make a good impression, being criticized for showing up late and missing team functions.{{Cite news|url=https://thebiglead.com/2018/07/10/celtics-rookie-robert-williams-draft-day-fall-suddenly-makes-perfect-sense/|title=Celtics Rookie Robert Williams' Draft Day Fall Suddenly Makes Perfect Sense|date=July 10, 2018|work=The Big Lead|access-date=July 12, 2018|archive-date=July 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723184920/https://thebiglead.com/2018/07/10/celtics-rookie-robert-williams-draft-day-fall-suddenly-makes-perfect-sense/|url-status=live}} His reputation for missing flights and video meetings caused him to earn the moniker "Time Lord" on online Boston Celtics fandoms.{{cite web |last=Leger |first=Justin |date=April 15, 2023 |orig-date=April 26, 2022 |title=Here's how Robert Williams earned 'Time Lord' nickname |url=https://www.nbcsportsboston.com/nba/boston-celtics/heres-how-robert-williams-earned-time-lord-nickname/208743/ |access-date=June 6, 2024 |publisher=[[NBC Sports Boston]]}}{{Cite web |last=DeCosta-Klipa |first=Nik |date=December 14, 2018 |title=Where did Robert Williams's nickname come from? |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2018/12/14/robert-williams-time-lord-nickname/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215062937/https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2018/12/14/robert-williams-time-lord-nickname |archive-date=December 15, 2018 |access-date=December 17, 2024 |website=boston.com}} Williams made his professional debut on October 23, 2018, playing four minutes during the Celtics' loss to [[Orlando Magic]], before being assigned to the [[Maine Red Claws]] on November 2. Throughout November and December, Williams split his time between the [[G League]] and the NBA, before starting to gain more game time with the Celtics following an injury to [[Al Horford]]. On December 11, 2018, Williams blocked two shots by [[NBA All Star]] [[Anthony Davis]] during a game against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2018/12/11/robert-williams-anthony-davis-block/|title=Sources: Robert Williams impresses in coming out party with the Celtics|work=boston.com|access-date=December 15, 2018|archive-date=December 17, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181217042349/https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2018/12/11/robert-williams-anthony-davis-block|url-status=live}} During the [[2021 NBA playoffs]], Williams dealt with a [[turf toe]] injury. In game 1 of the first-round series against the [[Brooklyn Nets]], Williams blocked 9 shots to set a team playoff record for blocks in a game. He also scored 11 points and grabbed 9 rebounds.{{cite news |last=Leger |first=Justin |title=Time Lord sets C's playoff record in Game 1 vs. Nets |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/celtics/robert-williams-sets-celtics-playoff-record-game-1-vs-nets |publisher=NBC Sports Boston |date=May 23, 2021 |access-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627224753/https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/celtics/robert-williams-sets-celtics-playoff-record-game-1-vs-nets |url-status=live }} Despite this record, the team lost the game. The injury hobbled Williams for the remainder of the series and Williams left game 3 with a sprained ankle after playing just 6 minutes.{{cite news |last=Vatour |first=Matt |title=Rob Williams injury: Boston Celtics big man sprains ankle, won't return |url=https://www.masslive.com/celtics/2021/05/rob-williams-injury-boston-celtics-big-man-sprains-ankle-wont-return.html |work=masslive |date=2021-05-29|access-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627224747/https://www.masslive.com/celtics/2021/05/rob-williams-injury-boston-celtics-big-man-sprains-ankle-wont-return.html |url-status=live }} He missed games 4 and 5, and the team lost the series 4–1. Following the season, Williams would sign a four-year, $54 million extension to keep him in Boston through the 2025–26 season.{{Cite web |date=August 20, 2021 |title=Boston Celtics, Robert Williams agree to four-year, $54M extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32056178 |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=ESPN.com |language=en|last=Bontemps|first=Tim}} On December 31, 2021, Williams recorded his first career [[triple-double]], putting up 10 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists, in a 123–108 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/celtics-news-how-robert-williams-surprised-ime-udoka-in-win-over-suns/|title=The reason Robert Williams surprised Ime Udoka in Celtics' win over Suns|website=ClutchPoints|last=DiGiovanni|first=Sam|date=December 31, 2021|access-date=December 31, 2021|archive-date=December 31, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211231235115/https://clutchpoints.com/celtics-news-how-robert-williams-surprised-ime-udoka-in-win-over-suns/|url-status=live}} On March 28, 2022, the Celtics announced that Williams had suffered a torn meniscus in his left knee and would be out indefinitely.{{Cite web |title=Celtics' Robert Williams III suffers torn meniscus in left knee, out indefinitely |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/celtics-robert-williams-iii-suffers-torn-meniscus-in-left-knee-out-indefinitely/ |access-date=March 28, 2022 |work=CBS Sports}} Two days later, he underwent surgery and was ruled out for at least four-to-six weeks.{{Cite web |title=Boston Celtics center Robert Williams III expected to miss 4-6 weeks after surgery to repair meniscus |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33629299 |access-date=March 30, 2022 |website=ESPN|date=March 30, 2022 |last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2023–present)=== ====2023–24==== On October 1, 2023, Williams, along with [[Malcolm Brogdon]] and two future first-round draft picks, was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Jrue Holiday]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Malcolm Brogdon and Robert Williams III|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-malcolm-brogdon-and-robert-williams-iii|website=NBA.com|date=October 1, 2023|access-date=October 1, 2023}} On October 25, Williams made his Trail Blazers debut, putting up 10 points and seven rebounds off the bench in a 123–111 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/veterans-guide-clippers-opening-win-over-blazers-2023-10-26/|title=Veterans guide Clippers to opening win over Blazers|website=Reuters|publisher=Field Level Media|date=October 26, 2023|access-date=October 26, 2023}} But his season was cut short, suffering a patellar dislocation after colliding with [[Jaren Jackson Jr.|Jaren Jackson Jr]]. on the Blazers' November 5 game against Memphis. Having successful right knee surgery a few days later, the injury ended his season after six games.{{Cite web |date=2023-11-13 |title=Robert Williams III Undergoes Right Knee Surgery |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/robert-williams-iii-undergoes-right-knee-surgery |access-date=2023-11-13 |website=NBA.com}} ====2024–25==== On September 30, 2024, Williams was cleared for training camp after coming off knee surgery.{{cite web |title=Trail Blazers' Robert Williams: Cleared for training camp |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trail-blazers-robert-williams-cleared-for-training-camp/ |website=CBSSports.com |access-date=30 September 2024 |language=en |date=30 September 2024}} On November 8, Williams made his return from injury putting up 13 points, three rebounds and two assists off the bench in a 127–102 loss against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. This game marked the first time he scored a [[three-pointer]] in his NBA career.{{Cite web |last=Holdahl |first=Casey |date=November 9, 2024 |title=Sharpe, Williams Return To The Court As The Blazers Return Home From A Four-Game Trip |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/sharpe-williams-return-to-the-court-as-the-blazers-return-home-from-a-four-game-trip |access-date=2024-11-09 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On November 25, Williams made his first start of the season as well as his first start as a member of the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] where he recorded 6 points, one assist and three rebounds in 12 minutes of action in a 123-98 loss against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], however during the 6:22 mark in second quarter, Williams dove hard for a loose ball and was whistled for a foul on Grizzlies guard [[Scotty Pippen Jr.]] and hit his head on the floor and took extra time trying to get up, but ended up remaining in the game until the 5:51 mark of the second quarter, but re-entered the game at the 2:31 mark and ended up playing for the remainder of the first half and then didn’t play in the second half and was later evaluated for a [[concussion]].{{Cite web |last=Bergin |first=Conor |date=2024-11-25 |title=Grant, Williams Exit Early vs. Grizzlies with Injuries |url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2024/11/25/24306193/portland-trail-blazers-memphis-grizzlies-nba-injury-news-robert-williams-jerami-grant |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=Blazer's Edge |language=en}} Williams made 20 total appearances (3 starts) for Portland during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 5.8 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.1 assists. On March 20, 2025, Williams underwent an [[arthroscopy]] to address inflammation in his left knee, necessitating a recovery timetable of four-to-six weeks and ruling him out for the remainder of the season.{{Cite web |date=March 21, 2025 |title=Blazers center Williams (knee) to miss 4-6 weeks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44336315 |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=ESPN.com |language=en|agency=Field Level Media}} ==== 2026–27 ==== On June 30, 2026, Williams re-signed with the Trail Blazers on a three-year, $44 million contract.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=June 30,
